solution: Divide both sides of \(24x < 100\) by 24. Since 24 is positive the direction of the inequality is unchanged: \(x < \frac{100}{24} = \frac{25}{6}\). Now \(\frac{25}{6} \approx 4.17\), so the natural numbers below it are \(1, 2, 3, 4\). Checking, \(24 \times 4 = 96 < 100\) while \(24 \times 5 = 120\) is not less than 100. Hence the solution set is \(\{1, 2, 3, 4\}\).

Dividing \(24x < 100\) by the positive number 24 keeps the direction: \(x < \frac{25}{6}\), and \(\frac{25}{6} \approx 4.17\). The integers below \(\frac{25}{6}\) are all integers up to and including 4, with no lower bound. Checking, \(x = 4\) gives \(96 < 100\) while \(x = 5\) gives \(120\), which fails. Hence the solution set is \(\{\ldots, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}\).

Divide both sides of \(-12x > 30\) by \(-12\). Dividing by a negative number REVERSES the inequality, so \(x < \frac{30}{-12} = -\frac{5}{2}\). Every natural number is positive, and no positive number is less than \(-\frac{5}{2}\); for instance \(x = 1\) gives \(-12\), which is not greater than 30. Hence no natural number satisfies the inequality, and the solution set is the empty set \(\varnothing\).

Dividing \(-12x > 30\) by \(-12\) reverses the inequality: \(x < -\frac{5}{2} = -2.5\). The integers less than \(-2.5\) are \(-3\) and everything below it. Checking, \(x = -3\) gives \(-12 \times (-3) = 36 > 30\), while \(x = -2\) gives \(24\), which fails. Hence the solution set is \(\{\ldots, -6, -5, -4, -3\}\).

From \(5x - 3 < 7\), add 3 to both sides: \(5x < 10\). Dividing by the positive number 5 keeps the direction, so \(x < 2\). Checking, \(x = 1\) gives \(2 < 7\) which holds, while \(x = 2\) gives \(7 < 7\) which fails. Hence the integer solutions are \(\{\ldots, -2, -1, 0, 1\}\).

From \(5x - 3 < 7\) we get \(5x < 10\), and dividing by the positive number 5 gives \(x < 2\). Checking, \(x = 0\) gives \(-3 < 7\) which holds, while \(x = 3\) gives \(12 < 7\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, 2)\).

From \(3x + 8 > 2\), subtract 8: \(3x > -6\). Dividing by the positive number 3 keeps the direction, so \(x > -2\). Checking, \(x = -1\) gives \(5 > 2\) which holds, while \(x = -2\) gives \(2 > 2\) which fails. Hence the integer solutions are \(\{-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots\}\).

From \(3x + 8 > 2\) we get \(3x > -6\), and dividing by the positive number 3 gives \(x > -2\). Checking, \(x = 0\) gives \(8 > 2\) which holds, while \(x = -3\) gives \(-1 > 2\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-2, \infty)\).

Collect the \(x\) terms on one side of \(4x + 3 < 5x + 7\): subtracting \(4x\) and 7 from both sides gives \(-4 < x\), that is \(x > -4\). No multiplication by a negative number was needed, so the direction is unchanged. Checking, \(x = 0\) gives \(3 < 7\) which holds, while \(x = -5\) gives \(-17 < -18\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-4, \infty)\).

From \(3x - 7 > 5x - 1\), subtract \(5x\) and add 7 to both sides: \(-2x > 6\). Dividing by \(-2\) REVERSES the inequality, giving \(x < -3\). Checking, \(x = -4\) gives \(-19 > -21\) which holds, while \(x = 0\) gives \(-7 > -1\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, -3)\).

Expand both sides of \(3(x - 1) \le 2(x - 3)\): \(3x - 3 \le 2x - 6\). Subtracting \(2x\) and adding 3 gives \(x \le -3\). Checking, \(x = -3\) gives \(-12 \le -12\) which holds, while \(x = 0\) gives \(-3 \le -6\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, -3]\).

Expand both sides of \(3(2 - x) \ge 2(1 - x)\): \(6 - 3x \ge 2 - 2x\). Adding \(3x\) and subtracting 2 gives \(4 \ge x\), that is \(x \le 4\); adding a term to both sides never changes the direction. Checking, \(x = 4\) gives \(-6 \ge -6\) which holds, while \(x = 5\) gives \(-9 \ge -8\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, 4]\).

The LCM of the denominators in \(x + \frac{x}{2} + \frac{x}{3} < 11\) is 6, and the left side becomes \(\frac{6x + 3x + 2x}{6} = \frac{11x}{6}\). So \(\frac{11x}{6} < 11\); multiplying by the positive number \(\frac{6}{11}\) keeps the direction and gives \(x < 6\). Checking, \(x = 0\) gives \(0 < 11\) which holds, while \(x = 6\) gives \(11 < 11\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, 6)\).

Multiply \(\frac{x}{3} > \frac{x}{2} + 1\) by the positive number 6: \(2x > 3x + 6\). Subtracting \(3x\) gives \(-x > 6\), and multiplying by \(-1\) REVERSES the inequality to \(x < -6\). Checking, \(x = -7\) gives \(-\frac{7}{3} \approx -2.33 > -2.5\) which holds, while \(x = -6\) gives \(-2 > -2\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, -6)\).

Multiply \(\frac{3(x - 2)}{5} \le \frac{5(2 - x)}{3}\) by the positive number 15: \(9(x - 2) \le 25(2 - x)\), that is \(9x - 18 \le 50 - 25x\). Adding \(25x\) and 18 gives \(34x \le 68\), so \(x \le 2\). Checking, \(x = 2\) gives \(0 \le 0\) which holds, while \(x = 3\) gives \(\frac{3}{5} \le -\frac{5}{3}\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, 2]\).

Multiply \(\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{3x}{5} + 4\right) \ge \frac{1}{3}(x - 6)\) by the positive number 30: \(15\left(\frac{3x}{5} + 4\right) \ge 10(x - 6)\), that is \(9x + 60 \ge 10x - 60\). Subtracting \(9x\) and adding 60 gives \(120 \ge x\), so \(x \le 120\). Checking, \(x = 120\) gives \(38 \ge 38\) which holds, while \(x = 150\) gives \(\frac{1}{2}(90 + 4) = 47 \ge \frac{1}{3}(144) = 48\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, 120]\).

Expand \(2(2x + 3) - 10 < 6(x - 2)\): \(4x + 6 - 10 < 6x - 12\), that is \(4x - 4 < 6x - 12\). Adding 12 and subtracting \(4x\) gives \(8 < 2x\), so \(x > 4\). Checking, \(x = 5\) gives \(16 < 18\) which holds, while \(x = 4\) gives \(12 < 12\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((4, \infty)\).

Simplify both sides of \(37 - (3x + 5) \ge 9x - 8(x - 3)\): the left becomes \(32 - 3x\) and the right becomes \(9x - 8x + 24 = x + 24\). So \(32 - 3x \ge x + 24\); adding \(3x\) and subtracting 24 gives \(8 \ge 4x\), so \(x \le 2\). Checking, \(x = 2\) gives \(26 \ge 26\) which holds, while \(x = 3\) gives \(23 \ge 27\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, 2]\).

Multiply \(\frac{x}{4} < \frac{5x - 2}{3} - \frac{7x - 3}{5}\) by the positive number 60: \(15x < 20(5x - 2) - 12(7x - 3)\), that is \(15x < 100x - 40 - 84x + 36 = 16x - 4\). Subtracting \(16x\) gives \(-x < -4\), and multiplying by \(-1\) REVERSES the inequality to \(x > 4\). Checking, \(x = 5\) gives \(1.25 < \frac{23}{3} - \frac{32}{5} \approx 1.27\) which holds, while \(x = 4\) gives \(1 < 6 - 5 = 1\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((4, \infty)\).

Multiply \(\frac{2x - 1}{3} \ge \frac{3x - 2}{4} - \frac{2 - x}{5}\) by the positive number 60: \(20(2x - 1) \ge 15(3x - 2) - 12(2 - x)\), that is \(40x - 20 \ge 45x - 30 - 24 + 12x = 57x - 54\). Adding 54 and subtracting \(40x\) gives \(34 \ge 17x\), so \(x \le 2\). Checking, \(x = 2\) gives \(1 \ge 1 - 0 = 1\) which holds, while \(x = 3\) gives \(\frac{5}{3} \approx 1.67 \ge \frac{7}{4} + \frac{1}{5} = 1.95\) which fails. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, 2]\).

From \(3x - 2 < 2x + 1\), subtract \(2x\) and add 2 to both sides: \(x < 3\). Checking, \(x = 2\) gives \(4 < 5\) which holds, while \(x = 3\) gives \(7 < 7\) which fails. On the number line, mark 3 with a hollow (unfilled) circle to show it is excluded, and darken the whole portion to the left of 3, continuing indefinitely. Hence the solution set is \((-\infty, 3)\).

From \(5x - 3 \ge 3x - 5\), subtract \(3x\) and add 3: \(2x \ge -2\), and dividing by the positive number 2 gives \(x \ge -1\). Checking, \(x = -1\) gives \(-8 \ge -8\) which holds, while \(x = -2\) gives \(-13 \ge -11\) which fails. On the number line, mark \(-1\) with a solid (filled) dot since it is included, and darken the portion to the right of \(-1\), continuing indefinitely. Hence the solution set is \([-1, \infty)\).

Expand \(3(1 - x) < 2(x + 4)\): \(3 - 3x < 2x + 8\). Adding \(3x\) and subtracting 8 gives \(-5 < 5x\), so \(x > -1\). Checking, \(x = 0\) gives \(3 < 8\) which holds, while \(x = -1\) gives \(6 < 6\) which fails. On the number line, mark \(-1\) with a hollow circle since it is excluded, and darken the portion to the right of \(-1\), continuing indefinitely. Hence the solution set is \((-1, \infty)\).

Multiply \(\frac{x}{2} \ge \frac{5x - 2}{3} - \frac{7x - 3}{5}\) by the positive number 30: \(15x \ge 10(5x - 2) - 6(7x - 3)\), that is \(15x \ge 50x - 20 - 42x + 18 = 8x - 2\). Subtracting \(8x\) gives \(7x \ge -2\), so \(x \ge -\frac{2}{7}\). Checking, \(x = 0\) gives \(0 \ge -\frac{2}{3} + \frac{3}{5} \approx -0.07\) which holds, while \(x = -1\) gives \(-0.5 \ge -\frac{7}{3} + 2 \approx -0.33\) which fails. On the number line, mark \(-\frac{2}{7}\) with a solid dot since it is included, and darken everything to its right. Hence the solution set is \(\left[-\frac{2}{7}, \infty\right)\).

Let \(x\) be the marks in the third test. The average of the three tests must be at least 60, so \(\frac{70 + 75 + x}{3} \ge 60\). Multiplying by the positive number 3 gives \(145 + x \ge 180\), so \(x \ge 35\). Checking, \(x = 35\) gives an average of \(\frac{180}{3} = 60\), which satisfies "at least 60", while \(x = 34\) gives \(\frac{179}{3} \approx 59.67\), which fails. Hence Ravi must score a minimum of 35 marks in the third test.

Let \(x\) be the marks in the fifth examination. The average of the five must be at least 90, so \(\frac{87 + 92 + 94 + 95 + x}{5} \ge 90\). The four known marks total 368, so \(368 + x \ge 450\), giving \(x \ge 82\). Checking, \(x = 82\) gives an average of \(\frac{450}{5} = 90\), which earns Grade A, while \(x = 81\) gives \(\frac{449}{5} = 89.8\), which fails. Hence Sunita must obtain a minimum of 82 marks in the fifth examination.

Let the pair be \(x\) and \(x + 2\) with \(x\) an odd positive integer. Both are smaller than 10, so \(x + 2 < 10\), giving \(x < 8\). Their sum exceeds 11, so \(x + (x + 2) > 11\), that is \(2x > 9\), giving \(x > \frac{9}{2} = 4.5\). Combining, \(4.5 < x < 8\) with \(x\) odd, so \(x = 5\) or \(x = 7\). Checking, \((5, 7)\) has sum 12 and \((7, 9)\) has sum 16, both more than 11 with both members under 10; the neighbouring pair \((3, 5)\) sums to only 8 and \((9, 11)\) has a member that is not smaller than 10, so both are rejected. Hence the required pairs are \((5, 7)\) and \((7, 9)\).

Let the pair be \(x\) and \(x + 2\) with \(x\) an even positive integer. Both are larger than 5, so \(x > 5\), and since \(x\) is even this means \(x \ge 6\). Their sum is less than 23, so \(x + (x + 2) < 23\), that is \(2x < 21\), giving \(x < 10.5\). Combining, \(6 \le x \le 10\) with \(x\) even, so \(x = 6, 8, 10\). Checking, \((10, 12)\) sums to 22 which is under 23, while the next pair \((12, 14)\) sums to 26 and is rejected, and \((4, 6)\) is rejected because 4 is not larger than 5. Hence the required pairs are \((6, 8)\), \((8, 10)\) and \((10, 12)\).

Let the shortest side be \(x\) cm. Then the longest side is \(3x\) cm and the third side is \((3x - 2)\) cm. The perimeter is at least 61 cm, so \(x + 3x + (3x - 2) \ge 61\), that is \(7x - 2 \ge 61\). Adding 2 gives \(7x \ge 63\), and dividing by the positive number 7 gives \(x \ge 9\). Checking, \(x = 9\) gives sides 9, 27, 25 with perimeter \(61 \ge 61\), which holds, while \(x = 8\) gives perimeter \(7(8) - 2 = 54\), which fails. Hence the minimum length of the shortest side is 9 cm.

Let the shortest piece be \(x\) cm. Then the second piece is \((x + 3)\) cm and the third is \(2x\) cm. The three pieces come from a board 91 cm long, so \(x + (x + 3) + 2x \le 91\), that is \(4x + 3 \le 91\), giving \(4x \le 88\) and \(x \le 22\). The third piece is at least 5 cm longer than the second, so \(2x \ge (x + 3) + 5\), that is \(2x \ge x + 8\), giving \(x \ge 8\). Both conditions must hold together, so \(8 \le x \le 22\). Checking, \(x = 8\) gives pieces 8, 11, 16 with total 35 cm and \(16 = 11 + 5\), which holds; \(x = 22\) gives 22, 25, 44 with total exactly 91 cm and \(44 \ge 30\), which holds; \(x = 7\) fails since \(14 < 15\), and \(x = 23\) fails since the total 95 cm exceeds the board. Hence the shortest board can have any length from 8 cm to 22 cm, that is \(8 \le x \le 22\).
_note: The printed Hint reads "then x, (x + 3) and 2x are the lengths of the second and third piece, respectively" — it lists THREE expressions while naming only two pieces (x is the shortest, not the second). The two inequalities that follow in the Hint are correct and are the ones used here; only the descriptive clause is misworded.

solution: Add 4 to each of the three parts of \(2 \le 3x - 4 \le 5\): \(6 \le 3x \le 9\). Dividing every part by the positive number 3 keeps both directions, giving \(2 \le x \le 3\). Checking, \(x = 2\) gives \(3x - 4 = 2\) and \(x = 3\) gives \(3x - 4 = 5\), both admissible, while \(x = 4\) gives \(3x - 4 = 8\), which exceeds 5 and fails. Hence the solution set is \([2, 3]\).

Expand the middle term of \(6 \le -3(2x - 4) < 12\) to get \(6 \le -6x + 12 < 12\). Subtracting 12 from each part gives \(-6 \le -6x < 0\). Now divide every part by \(-6\); dividing by a negative number REVERSES both directions, giving \(1 \ge x > 0\), that is \(0 < x \le 1\). Checking, \(x = 1\) gives \(-3(-2) = 6\), which satisfies \(6 \le 6 < 12\); \(x = 0\) gives 12, which is not less than 12 and so is excluded; \(x = 2\) gives 0, which fails. Hence the solution set is \((0, 1]\).

Subtract 4 from each part of \(-3 \le 4 - \frac{7x}{2} \le 18\): \(-7 \le -\frac{7x}{2} \le 14\). Multiply every part by \(-\frac{2}{7}\); since this factor is negative both directions REVERSE, giving \(2 \ge x \ge -4\), that is \(-4 \le x \le 2\). Checking, \(x = 2\) gives \(4 - 7 = -3\) and \(x = -4\) gives \(4 + 14 = 18\), both admissible, while \(x = 3\) gives \(-6.5\), which is below \(-3\) and fails. Hence the solution set is \([-4, 2]\).

Multiply each part of \(-15 < \frac{3(x - 2)}{5} \le 0\) by the positive number \(\frac{5}{3}\), which keeps both directions: \(-25 < x - 2 \le 0\). Adding 2 to each part gives \(-23 < x \le 2\). Checking, \(x = 2\) gives 0, which satisfies \(-15 < 0 \le 0\); \(x = -22\) gives \(\frac{3(-24)}{5} = -14.4\), which lies in range; \(x = -23\) gives exactly \(-15\), which is not greater than \(-15\) and so is excluded, and \(x = 3\) gives \(0.6\), which exceeds 0 and fails. Hence the solution set is \((-23, 2]\).

First simplify the middle term: \(4 - \frac{3x}{-5} = 4 + \frac{3x}{5}\), so the inequality is \(-12 < 4 + \frac{3x}{5} \le 2\). Subtracting 4 from each part gives \(-16 < \frac{3x}{5} \le -2\). Multiplying every part by the positive number \(\frac{5}{3}\) keeps both directions, giving \(-\frac{80}{3} < x \le -\frac{10}{3}\). Checking, \(x = -\frac{10}{3}\) gives \(4 - 2 = 2\), which is admissible; \(x = -10\) gives \(4 - 6 = -2\), which lies in range; \(x = -\frac{80}{3}\) gives exactly \(-12\), which is not greater than \(-12\) and so is excluded, and \(x = -30\) gives \(-14\), which fails. Hence the solution set is \(\left(-\frac{80}{3}, -\frac{10}{3}\right]\).

Multiply each part of \(7 \le \frac{3x + 11}{2} \le 11\) by the positive number 2: \(14 \le 3x + 11 \le 22\). Subtracting 11 from each part gives \(3 \le 3x \le 11\), and dividing by the positive number 3 gives \(1 \le x \le \frac{11}{3}\). Checking, \(x = 1\) gives \(\frac{14}{2} = 7\) and \(x = \frac{11}{3}\) gives \(\frac{22}{2} = 11\), both admissible, while \(x = 4\) gives \(\frac{23}{2} = 11.5\), which exceeds 11 and fails. Hence the solution set is \(\left[1, \frac{11}{3}\right]\).

Solve each inequality separately. From \(5x + 1 > -24\), subtracting 1 gives \(5x > -25\), so \(x > -5\). From \(5x - 1 < 24\), adding 1 gives \(5x < 25\), so \(x < 5\). Both must hold, so the solution is the intersection \(-5 < x < 5\). Checking, \(x = 0\) satisfies \(1 > -24\) and \(-1 < 24\); \(x = 5\) fails the second since \(24 < 24\) is false, and \(x = -5\) fails the first since \(-24 > -24\) is false. On the number line, mark \(-5\) and 5 with hollow circles and darken the segment strictly between them. Hence the solution set is \((-5, 5)\).

Solve each inequality separately. From \(2(x - 1) < x + 5\) we get \(2x - 2 < x + 5\), so \(x < 7\). From \(3(x + 2) > 2 - x\) we get \(3x + 6 > 2 - x\), so \(4x > -4\) and \(x > -1\). Both must hold, so the solution is the intersection \(-1 < x < 7\). Checking, \(x = 0\) satisfies \(-2 < 5\) and \(6 > 2\); \(x = 7\) fails the first since \(12 < 12\) is false, and \(x = -1\) fails the second since \(3 > 3\) is false. On the number line, mark \(-1\) and 7 with hollow circles and darken the segment strictly between them. Hence the solution set is \((-1, 7)\).

Solve each inequality separately. From \(3x - 7 > 2(x - 6)\) we get \(3x - 7 > 2x - 12\), so \(x > -5\). From \(6 - x > 11 - 2x\), adding \(2x\) and subtracting 6 gives \(x > 5\). Both must hold, and since every number greater than 5 is already greater than \(-5\), the intersection is \(x > 5\). Checking, \(x = 6\) satisfies \(11 > 0\) and \(0 > -1\); \(x = 5\) fails the second since \(1 > 1\) is false, and \(x = 0\) fails it as well since \(6 > 11\) is false. On the number line, mark 5 with a hollow circle and darken everything to its right. Hence the solution set is \((5, \infty)\).

Solve each inequality separately. From \(5(2x - 7) - 3(2x + 3) \le 0\) we get \(10x - 35 - 6x - 9 \le 0\), that is \(4x \le 44\), so \(x \le 11\). From \(2x + 19 \le 6x + 47\), subtracting \(2x\) and 47 gives \(-28 \le 4x\), so \(x \ge -7\). Both must hold, so the solution is \(-7 \le x \le 11\). Checking, \(x = 11\) gives \(75 - 75 = 0 \le 0\) and \(41 \le 113\); \(x = -7\) gives \(-105 + 33 = -72 \le 0\) and \(5 \le 5\); \(x = 12\) fails the first since \(4 \le 0\) is false, and \(x = -8\) fails the second since \(3 \le -1\) is false. On the number line, mark \(-7\) and 11 with solid dots and darken the segment joining them. Hence the solution set is \([-7, 11]\).

The solution is kept between \(68^\circ\ \text{F}\) and \(77^\circ\ \text{F}\), so \(68 < \text{F} < 77\). Substituting \(\text{F} = \frac{9}{5}\text{C} + 32\) gives \(68 < \frac{9}{5}\text{C} + 32 < 77\). Subtracting 32 from each part gives \(36 < \frac{9}{5}\text{C} < 45\), and multiplying every part by the positive number \(\frac{5}{9}\) keeps both directions, giving \(20 < \text{C} < 25\). Checking, \(\text{C} = 22\) gives \(\text{F} = 71.6\), which lies in range, while \(\text{C} = 20\) gives exactly \(68^\circ\ \text{F}\) and \(\text{C} = 30\) gives \(86^\circ\ \text{F}\), neither of which lies strictly between the two limits. Hence the temperature range is \(20^\circ\ \text{C}\) to \(25^\circ\ \text{C}\), that is \(20 < \text{C} < 25\).

Let \(x\) litres of the 2% solution be added to 640 litres of the 8% solution. The mixture then has volume \((640 + x)\) litres and contains \(\frac{8}{100}(640) + \frac{2}{100}x = 51.2 + 0.02x\) litres of boric acid. The requirement is \(4\% < \text{acid} < 6\%\) of the mixture. From \(51.2 + 0.02x > 0.04(640 + x)\) we get \(51.2 + 0.02x > 25.6 + 0.04x\), so \(25.6 > 0.02x\) and \(x < 1280\). From \(51.2 + 0.02x < 0.06(640 + x)\) we get \(51.2 + 0.02x < 38.4 + 0.06x\), so \(12.8 < 0.04x\) and \(x > 320\). Checking, \(x = 640\) gives 64 litres of acid in 1280 litres, that is 5%, which lies in range; \(x = 320\) gives 57.6 litres in 960 litres, exactly 6%, which is excluded, and \(x = 1280\) gives 76.8 litres in 1920 litres, exactly 4%, also excluded. Hence the amount added must satisfy \(320 < x < 1280\), that is more than 320 litres but less than 1280 litres.

Let \(x\) litres of water be added to 1125 litres of the 45% acid solution. The acid quantity stays fixed at \(\frac{45}{100}(1125) = 506.25\) litres while the volume becomes \((1125 + x)\) litres. From the requirement that the acid content exceeds 25%, \(506.25 > 0.25(1125 + x)\), that is \(506.25 > 281.25 + 0.25x\), so \(225 > 0.25x\) and \(x < 900\). From the requirement that it is below 30%, \(506.25 < 0.30(1125 + x)\), that is \(506.25 < 337.5 + 0.3x\), so \(168.75 < 0.3x\) and \(x > 562.5\). Checking, \(x = 700\) gives \(\frac{506.25}{1825} \approx 27.7\%\), which lies in range; \(x = 562.5\) gives exactly 30% and \(x = 900\) gives exactly 25%, both excluded, and \(x = 1000\) gives about 23.8%, which fails. Hence the water added must satisfy \(562.5 < x < 900\), that is more than 562.5 litres but less than 900 litres.

For these children \(\text{CA} = 12\) years, so \(\text{IQ} = \frac{\text{MA}}{12} \times 100 = \frac{25\,\text{MA}}{3}\). The condition \(80 \le \text{IQ} \le 140\) becomes \(80 \le \frac{25\,\text{MA}}{3} \le 140\). Multiplying every part by the positive number \(\frac{3}{25}\) keeps both directions, giving \(9.6 \le \text{MA} \le 16.8\). Checking, \(\text{MA} = 9.6\) gives \(\text{IQ} = 80\) and \(\text{MA} = 16.8\) gives \(\text{IQ} = 140\), both admissible, while \(\text{MA} = 17\) gives \(\text{IQ} \approx 141.7\), which fails. Hence the mental age lies in the range \(9.6 \le \text{MA} \le 16.8\) years.
